name: Claudius
title: Roman Emperor
summary: Claudius was the fourth Roman emperor, reigning from 41 to 54 AD. He is mentioned in the New Testament in connection with a severe famine that struck the entire Roman Empire, and for his edict expelling all Jews from Rome, which directly affected early Christian movements, including Aquila and Priscilla.

keyEvents.title: The Famine under Claudius
keyEvents.description: The prophet Agabus predicted a severe famine that would strike the whole world, and this famine occurred during the reign of Emperor Claudius.

keyEvents.title: Expulsion of Jews from Rome
keyEvents.description: Claudius ordered all Jews to leave Rome, which led Aquila and Priscilla to move to Corinth, where they met the apostle Paul.

keyEvents.title: Paul Meets Aquila and Priscilla in Corinth
keyEvents.description: As a direct result of Claudius' expulsion edict, Aquila and Priscilla came to Corinth, where they became important co-workers with Paul in his missionary work.

keyEvents.title: Help for the Brothers in Judea
keyEvents.description: In response to Agabus' prophecy about the famine under Claudius, the disciples in Antioch collected funds and sent help to the believers in Judea through Barnabas and Saul.
